chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), in the hadith of Barirah,
that the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said to Aisha: 'Emancipate (her), for the guardianship (walayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.أَعْتِقِي: Emancipate; imperative verb referring to freeing a slave.
key_terms.الْوَلَاءَ: Guardianship or manumission bond; the legal relationship of authority a master retains over a freed slave.
key_terms.بَرِيرَةَ: Barirah; a famous slave woman whose emancipation case was discussed by the Prophet and Imams.

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of guardianship over a freed slave according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Zurarah from Imam al-Baqir, confirms the Prophet’s directive to Aisha regarding Barirah, establishing 'al-wala' as the legal bond of guardianship transferring to the manumitter. It serves as a foundational proof in Shia jurisprudence for the rights of the owner over the freed slave, emphasizing the social and economic implications of emancipation within the family structure.
